Cyber Attack Disrupts Payment Systems and Telecommunications Across Peru

LIMA, June 7 — A large-scale cyber attack on Peru’s payment networks and telecommunications sector disrupted economic activity nationwide Friday, leaving businesses unable to process digital transactions and many citizens without reliable phone or internet service.

The attack, which began late Thursday evening, targeted the electronic payment clearinghouse and several major telecom exchanges, according to the National Authority for Digital Security (ANDS). As of Friday afternoon, the incident remained ongoing, with intermittent outages reported in Lima, Arequipa, Trujillo and other major cities.

“We are experiencing a coordinated and sophisticated cyber event impacting critical infrastructure,” said ANDS director Rosa del Castillo at a press briefing. “Our teams are working around the clock to contain the threat and restore services.”

Retailers and banks were among the hardest hit, as customers struggled to make purchases or withdraw cash. The Peruvian Chamber of Commerce said that point-of-sale terminals using the PayPeru and InterRed networks were offline for hours, forcing many stores to accept cash only.

“We have never seen such a widespread failure of payment systems,” said Luis Gamarra, president of the chamber. “This is severely affecting daily commerce, especially for small businesses that rely on electronic transactions.”

Mobile networks operated by Celeris and AndinaTel also experienced outages, causing dropped calls and loss of internet connectivity for millions. The National Telecommunications Union urged operators to prioritize emergency communications and restore service as soon as possible.

Analysts warned that the disruption could have a lasting impact on confidence in Peru’s digital infrastructure. “This event highlights the vulnerability of our interconnected economy,” said Alicia Torres, a cybersecurity analyst at the Lima Policy Institute. “It’s crucial that authorities not only resolve the immediate crisis but invest in long-term resilience.”

Officials have not attributed the attack to any group or country, but said investigations are underway. The Ministry of Economy estimated that business losses could reach tens of millions of dollars if the disruption continues into the weekend.
